deep.reconstruction:
The upper half of the page is a plan for the November–December 1967 IHES lectures on crystals. These lectures were written up by I. Coates and O. Jussila as 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', in Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968). The plan has eight sections:
- §1: ordinary de Rham cohomology.
- §2: a survey of l-adic cohomology and the motivation for a p-adic cohomology in characteristic p.
- §3: an exposé ('topo') on Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology.
- §4: stratifications, and how Monsky–Washnitzer relates to the Gauss–Manin connection on de Rham cohomology.
- §5: the crystalline and stratifying sites, with a theorem and a conjecture in characteristic 0.
- §6: Čech computations in any characteristic.
- §7: comparison of de Rham and crystalline cohomology in characteristic 0.
- §8: return to characteristic p > 0.

The lower half begins §6.1 ('Coh. stratifiante'). We work on the stratifying site of X/S. Its objects are pairs (U,X') with U ⊂ X open and U → X' a nilpotent thickening over S, subject to the restriction that X' locally retracts onto X.

Let X̃ be the sheaf (U,X') ↦ {S-morphisms X' → X extending U → X}. The restriction on objects is exactly what makes X̃ → e an epimorphism, i.e. X̃ covers the final object. (Grothendieck notes this is where the stratifying site differs from the crystalline site.)

The Čech–Leray spectral sequence of this covering is
E_2^{pq} = H^p(ν ↦ H^q(X̃^{ν+1}, F)) ⇒ H^*(X_strat, F).

The (ν+1)-fold product X̃^{ν+1} in the topos is the ind-object colim_i Δ_X^{(ν)}(i). Here Δ_X^{(ν)}(i) is the i-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of the diagonal in X^{ν+1} (over S), viewed as an object (X, Δ^{(ν)}(i)) of the site. For a representable object one has H^*((U,X'),F) = H^*(X', F_{(U,X')}).

The next page continues the argument. Assume X affine and the F_{Δ(i)} quasi-coherent and Mittag-Leffler. Then the higher cohomology of X̃^{ν+1} vanishes and H^0 = lim_i F(Δ^{(ν)}(i)). Hence H^*(X_strat, F) is computed by the cosimplicial complex of F evaluated on the formal completions of X^{ν+1} along the diagonal: the 'Čech–Alexander' computation.

The purpose is the characteristic-0 comparison: stratifying/crystalline cohomology of O equals de Rham cohomology (via linearization / the Poincaré lemma). It is also a template for the characteristic-p computations.
errors: No mathematical error. Grothendieck writes 'prosystème' for the system of the Δ^{(ν)}(i). As geometric objects these form an ind-system (a pro-system of rings), and X̃^{ν+1} is a colimit in the topos. This is a terminological looseness, consistent with his writing lim→.
The identification of H^q of the colimit with lim H^q(Δ(i)) needs a Mittag-Leffler/lim^1 argument. This is not stated on this page but is added on the next page.

ideas.what: Outline of the 1967 IHES lectures on crystals: l-adic motivation, Monsky–Washnitzer, stratifications vs Gauss–Manin, crystalline vs stratifying site, Čech computations, de Rham comparison in characteristic 0
ideas.modern_name: Plan of 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes'
ideas.where_published: Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas, exposé IX

ideas.what: The object X̃ (sheaf represented by X) covers the final object of the stratifying topos, giving a Čech–Leray spectral sequence
ideas.modern_name: Čech–Alexander / Leray spectral sequence for the infinitesimal-stratifying site
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck 1968; developed by Berthelot (thesis, 1974) and Berthelot–Ogus
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, §§5–6

deep.surprise_reason: This is the preparatory plan and draft of §6 of the 1967 crystals lectures. Both match the published Coates–Jussila notes closely. It is of archival interest as a draft, but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Topo[?] de Washnitzer-Monsky' – 'Topo' (French slang for an exposé) appears correct; no 's'.
Margin label at 6.1 reads 'Coh. stratifiante', a section heading written beside crossed-out words.
'Donc pour ici [?] avons' probably reads 'Donc nous avons' (or 'Donc nous aurons').
'considéré comme prosystème au-dessus de X' is likely plural: 'considérés comme prosystèmes au-dessus de X', followed by the diagram X ← U → X' and the label (U,X').
Parenthesis likely reads '(c'est ici qu'on utilise la restriction sur les objets du site stratifiant [par rapport au] site cristallin)'.
